checksums.name: header_sum16_negated
checksums.formula_detail: stored = (-(sum of the other seven 16-bit words)) mod 65536; valid iff sum of all eight words == 0 mod 65536 (FUN_080457f4). On .sav file bytes words must be taken byte-swapped (big-endian per word) due to the serial EEPROM driver (FUN_080522c0/FUN_080521ec); little-endian file interpretation fails with total 0x00fe. Stored field zeroed before computing.

checksums.name: slot_sum16_negated
checksums.formula_detail: Same FUN_080457f4 routine over 80 bytes (40 words); FUN_08045690 zeroes slot+0x4e, stores -sum there; FUN_08045780 validates total sum == 0. File byte-lane caveat as header checksum.

io_driver_functions.notes: DMA3 transfer engine: programs src/dst/count (count|0x80000000) via literal-pool MMIO pointers, polls completion; used for both EEPROM directions
EEPROM 8-byte block read: builds start/read/address bitstream, DMA out width+3, DMA in 0x44 units, reassembles 4 u16 MSB-first in reverse word order
EEPROM 8-byte block write: start/write/address+64 data bits LSB-first per u16, DMA width+0x43, busy-poll with timeout
Wrapper: tail-calls FUN_080522c0(addr,data,1)
EEPROM verify: read-back via FUN_080521ec and compare 4 u16; returns 0 match / 0x8000 mismatch
EEPROM config select; called with 4 for this game (sets block count / address width in shared config struct)
Transfer prologue: saves DMA regs, calls FUN_08052124(4)
Transfer epilogue: restores DMA regs saved by FUN_0800b42c
Byte-level EEPROM read: offset/len >>3 to 8-byte blocks, up to 3 retries per block via FUN_080521ec
Byte-level EEPROM write+verify per 8-byte block via FUN_080522ac + FUN_08052450, up to 3 retries
Sum of len/2 u16 words truncated to 16 bits (also inlined in FUN_08045404/FUN_08045874)
Create default header from ROM template, store -sum at +0x0e, write both header copies
Validate one header copy: EEPROM read (block<<3), zero-sum test, then 8-byte magic compare
Header load: primary block 0 else mirror block 0x3e (offset 0x1f0); copies survivor over failed RAM half
Header flush: recompute checksum at RAM +0x0e/+0x1e, word-compare RAM vs both EEPROM copies, rewrite both on mismatch
Slot read: FUN_0800b34c(0x10+slot*0x50, 0x50, manager+0x20 buffer)
Slot write: FUN_0800b3b4(0x10+slot*0x50, 0x50, manager+0x20 buffer)
Slot validate: manager+0x54+slot = (FUN_080457f4(slotbuf,0x50)==0)
Prepare slot buffer: zero 0x50, optionally pack via missing func_0x0802d40c (flag==0), store checksum at +0x4e
Write logical profile p and backup p+3, read back, validate, unpack/zero descriptor, record p in header byte 11
Boot load/repair of all 6 physical slots from paired copies; unpack descriptors via FUN_0802d670
Unpack slot payload bytes 0-7 into 8-byte manager descriptor with permuted byte order via FUN_0804554c
Slot-buffer unpack cursor copy (manager+0x5c cursor, +0x60 skip flag)
Pack six state bytes (+0x15,+0x17,+0x18,+0x19,+0x1a,+0x1b) into RAM header, copy to RAM mirror, flush via FUN_08045360
Unpack header bytes 8,9,10,12,13 back into state struct (byte 11 not read)

open_questions: Absolute RAM addresses of the header area and save-manager struct: all globals are literal-pool _DAT_080xxxxx pointers whose values are absent from ghidra/decompiled.c, so ram_addr is null throughout
Slot payload bytes 8-77 (70 of 80 bytes): the live-state packer func_0x0802d40c called by FUN_08045690 is not among the 280 traced functions, and both samples have all slots zeroed
Semantics of header bytes 8, 9, 12 and of the state-struct fields (+0x15,+0x17,+0x18,+0x19,+0x1a) they mirror; byte 10 is a <6 index (language hypothesis unproven)
Header byte 11 is 0x00 in both samples although both traced writers set bit 0 or slot bits; an untraced writer/flush path must also update the header
No traced caller for top-level entry points FUN_08045454, FUN_0803d208, FUN_0802d5bc (presumed function-pointer/state-machine dispatch reported as UNRECOVERED_JUMPTABLE)
ghidra/callgraph.json omits most func_0x (tail-call) edges; caller chains were rebuilt from decompiled body text and the two sources were cross-checked where both exist

The apparent sum8 identity at header byte 12 (-sum(bytes0..8) mod 256) cannot be distinguished from the proven sum16 checksum with only two samples differing in bytes 8/12; no byte-sum routine exists in the code
No paired .ss save states were provided (states/ is empty), so all fuzzing predictions in section 6 are untested

EEPROM config values (block count at config+4, address width at config+8) set by FUN_08052124(4) are behind _DAT_ pointers; 64 blocks x 8 bytes = 512 B is inferred from geometry and transfers, not read directly
